title: Design Systems: how to build and maintain a scalable design system
description: How to build and maintain a scalable design system: benefits, a step-by-step way to start small, clear documentation and ongoing governance.

blocks.text: Hi there, Product Designers, UX/UI Designers and interface lovers!

If your design and development team is growing fast, you've probably run into inconsistencies that hurt productivity: buttons with different styles, misaligned spacing, fonts that don't get along… Chaos can set in at any moment! The fix? A well-structured design system.

data.title: Buttons with different styles
data.body: Flip the switch and see the same set of buttons without and with a design system.

blocks.text: This set of guidelines and components not only guarantees visual and functional consistency, it also cuts costs and speeds up development. In this article, let's have a relaxed chat about how to build and maintain a scalable design system, with practical examples and essential tips you can apply today.

items: Implementing a design system brings a series of advantages that directly affect the daily work of designers and developers. Here are some of the benefits:
Less rework: A real example is Airbnb, which managed to cut the time spent creating interfaces by 50% after adopting a design system. With predefined components, duplicated effort drops considerably.
Scalability: Giants like Google and Uber use standardized systems to make sure that, regardless of the project or the team, the user experience is consistent worldwide.
Faster development: By reusing components, the time to create new screens can drop by up to 30%. That means more focus on innovation and less time on operational tweaks.

blocks.text: How to build a design system
Building a solid design system can feel challenging, but with a clear step-by-step, you can turn it into a light and efficient process:

blocks.caption: A system grows in layers: start at the base and work your way up.

items: Define the essential elements: Start by choosing colors, typography, spacing and basic components like buttons, forms and cards.
Focus on what matters: Instead of trying to build a complete system all at once, build a solid foundation and add to it over time.
Practical example: Think about your current project and identify which elements are used most often. Start there!

data.title: Start small: the basic decisions
data.body: Color, typography, spacing, radius and shadow are layers that, together, make up every component.

items: Guidelines and best practices: Record everything on collaborative platforms like Figma, Zeroheight or Notion. Detailed documentation makes sure everyone on the team follows the same rules.
Visual and accessible: Use visual examples and keep the documentation up to date so the system evolves with the project's needs.
Friendly tip: Do periodic reviews to include new findings and adjustments suggested by the team.
Governance is essential: Without constant management, your design system can turn into a “graveyard” of outdated components.
Owner team: Define a team or a person responsible for reviewing and updating components.
Constant feedback: Encourage communication between designers and developers to spot and fix inconsistencies quickly.

blocks.caption: Without governance, the system becomes a component graveyard.

blocks.text: The healthiest way to organize a design system today is to split tokens into layers. The primitive holds the raw value, the semantic token says what it's for, and the component uses the semantic one.

blocks.caption: Change the primitive, the semantic token passes it along and every component follows, no hunting color by color.

blocks.text: The W3C Design Tokens Community Group has been standardizing a common format for tokens. That makes it easier to carry the same decision from Figma to code and to other tools.

And there's a new reason to care about this: AI tools generate much better interfaces when they get the design system as context. Well-documented components, tokens and rules cut down on generic output.
blocks.lead: Design system as context for AI:

blocks.text: Make the design system part of the company culture

A design system isn't just a set of components, it's a philosophy the whole team needs to embrace. By encouraging collaboration and consistent use of the guidelines, you create a more organized and efficient work environment, where every detail contributes to a better user experience.
